svg.title: Seven new wires from Raspberry Pi to motor driver, power disconnected
svg.desc: All numbers physical. Pi USB ports at top and header at left. Driver heatsink at top; use six outer signal pins, avoid two inner 5 volt posts. Common ground from spare breakout minus to physical14.
svg.text: L298N MOTOR CONTROL AND COMMON GROUND
FIRST: shut down the Pi, then unplug its USB-C power. Motor wall adapter stays unplugged.
Leave the sensor wires connected. Use 7 jumper wires with a hollow socket at BOTH ends.
All numbers below are PHYSICAL pin positions, not GPIO / BCM numbers.
1 PI: USB SOCKETS AT THE TOP
Components face up. Long pin header on the LEFT.
BOTTOM PAIR: physical 2 on left • physical 1 on right
Grey pins 2, 6, 18 and 22: existing sensor wires stay put.
Use the continuous row nearest the board’s OUTER EDGE.
Leave these 2 inner posts EMPTY (+5 V).
USE THIS OUTER ROW — alongside the printed labels
All three removed jumper caps stay OFF.
Wire colours are suggestions. Match BOTH ends by pin.
The new ground wire uses a FREE − pin; keep the existing black wire.
HOW TO PLUG EACH NEW WIRE
One hollow socket goes over one metal pin. The other socket goes over its matching Pi pin.
On ENA and ENB, use the pin closest to the printed label / outer edge. Leave the inner pin empty.
No motor-supply positive wire connects to the Pi. Common ground is the black wire to pin 14.
Trace all six signal wires by their labels and verify the shared ground. Keep both supplies unplugged.
For the first motor test, keep wheels clear of the bench and pulse one motor at a time.
Reference orientation drawings • exact pin numbering • not to scale
Existing motor wires and distance-sensor wiring stay connected.
